title: The neighbourhood where Picou's mother lived and parties there
summary: He mentions an old composition and recalls Picou's mother living nearby, and the house parties with piano and singing.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: But I'll tell you what I'm doing though. I have a composition that I'd throw on the side. I'd throw that composition on the side because at that time I didn't think anything of it. But you see, T. K. Huerta called man, he had a brother by the name of Uris. A singer. He had some kind of a band. He used to go around, a little routine band. I never got to know him.
I'm sorry. I always... Well, he died too. Yes, I heard about him.

Right here in the next block. You happen to be right in the neighborhood where these things took place. In the next block, the Claiborne hardware store bought out two Devil Cottages on Robinson Street to extend their business all the way through from Robinson to Claiborne. Well, those two Devil Cottages, Piku's mother lived in one of them at the time. And a friend of mine, Jean-Marie, his mother lived there. And on account of coming there with him, I found out that Piku's mother was living there in the neighborhood. Yes. Now, next door to Piku, there was a lady that was really friendly with her and had a piano. And when they found out that I'd come around there with my friend and say, well, come play. In those days, it was a great thing to go there and you'd play, they'd dance, they'd sing, you understand? And make a supper and so forth, and that was entertainment, you know? That was much entertainment. So I used to go off the road. . . .
